title: Stripping Diagnostics from Parser Errors
pattern: Throwing an error with only a textual description while discarding the physical location (span, line number, or index) where the parsing failure occurred.
why_bad: It destroys debug context. Developers and operators cannot determine where in the file or input payload the syntax error happened, forcing painful and slow manual analysis.
detection: Parsing logic returning an error type that lacks index, span, or position fields.
counterexample:
Errors where physical position has no meaning:
```rust
fn divide(a: i32, b: i32) -> Result<i32, DivByZeroError> { ... }
```
fix:
Return a structured error that carries the exact span or file location of the fault.
```rust
struct ParseError {
    message: String,
    line: usize,
    column: usize,
}
```
source: *Types and Programming Languages* by Benjamin C. Pierce (p. 13, info parameter); *Rust for Rustaceans* by Jon Gjengset (p. 142-143, spans).
